newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares drop, still uneasy on politics.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares drop, still uneasy on politics.

text.p: Istanbul shares lost an average 1.1 percent on Wednesday amid political uneasiness which persisted although parliament voted on Tuesday not to proceed with a censure motion against the Islamist-led government.
The IMKB National-100 closed down 18 points at 1,623 after falling from an early high of 1,649. Brokers were expecting resistance at 1,650 after the index rose 1.6 percent in the last two days.
Trade volume shrank to 20.88 trillion lira from 30.21 trillion on Tuesday.
"Trade remained in a narrow range and volume fell because the market awaits Friday's National Security Council meeting," said Haydar Haydaroglu from state-owned Halkbank.

Tension is expected to be high at Friday's meeting to be attended by chiefs of the secularist military and Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan because of recent public squabbling between the generals and the Islamist wing of the coalition.
Brokers said buying of shares of largely state owned firms which are highly capitalised prevented a further fall.
"The market is uneasy and needs concrete developments in privatisation and economic issues to get a boost," said Haydaroglu.

Of the 238 shares traded, losers outdid gainers sharply by 160 to 41 and 37 closed stable. The IMKB Industrial dropped 0.95 percent to 1,662, the IMKB Services fell 1.68 percent to 1,463 and the IMKB Financial was down 1.4 percent to 1,689.

Leading actives were largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, up 250 lira at 22,000, largely state-owned petroleum refiner Tupras, up 3,000 lira at 64,000 and steel rope producer Celik Halat, steady at 8,300 lira. They made up 19.2 percent of the total turnover.
